elements.element: Preferred: no non-solicitation obligation binding Customer
elements.evidence: delete_paragraph p0045 removes "Customer shall not solicit... any Vendor employee"

elements.element: Preferred: no no-hire/no-employment restriction binding Customer
elements.evidence: deleted text included "hire, or employ any Vendor employee" and "regardless of how the employee applies"

elements.element: Preferred: no residual post-term solicitation restriction on Customer
elements.evidence: deleted "during the term or for twenty-four months afterward"; no replacement restriction inserted

elements.element: Fallback: mutual non-solicit obligation binding both Parties
elements.evidence: clause deleted in full; no mutual undertaking substituted

elements.element: Fallback: scope limited to personnel directly involved in the Services
elements.evidence: no scope language remains after deletion

elements.element: Fallback: 12 months from end of involvement
elements.evidence: duration language removed rather than reduced to 12 months

elements.element: Fallback: carve-outs for general advertisements and unsolicited approaches
elements.evidence: no carve-out inserted; whole paragraph removed

reasons: The locked target is the preferred position — no non-solicit binding Customer — and deleting § 12.4 in its entirety is the only edit that achieves it; partial word-level surgery could not reach 'no non-solicit'.

The deterministic minimality gate objects to whole-paragraph deletion, but here the paragraph is the offending obligation itself, so the deletion is the minimum change; no replacement or extra wording was added.

The official checks for a 12-month duration and a general-solicitation carve-out are fallback-only elements and are correctly absent at the preferred level; they should not be scored against this redline.

Intent is preserved and improved: removal eliminates the contradiction with § 12.3 (Vendor's acknowledgement that Customer made no no-hire commitment) and leaves no dangling cross-reference or undefined term.
